--- title: Marginal Effects and Hypothesis Tests via `marginaleffects` description: "Compute average and subgroup marginal effects and run linear and non-linear hypothesis tests on fitted PyFixest models." aliases: - /marginaleffects.html format: html: html-table-processing: none toc: true toc-title: "On this page" toc-location: left freeze: auto --- `PyFixest` integrates with the excellent [marginaleffects](https://github.com/vincentarelbundock/pymarginaleffects) package. Among many other things, `marginaleffects` allows you to compute: - average marginal effects, - subgroup marginal effects, - linear and non-linear hypothesis tests. ::: {#4b4faf37 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import numpy as np from marginaleffects import avg_slopes, hypotheses import pyfixest as pf data = pf.get_data() data["Y_bin"] = np.where(data["Y"] > 0, 1, 0) fit = pf.feglm("Y_bin ~ X1 + X2 | f1", data=data, family="logit") fit.tidy() ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ```{=html}

``` ::: ::: ## Average marginal effects To compute the average marginal effect of `X1` on the response scale: ::: {#d6426b05 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} avg_slopes(fit, variables="X1") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ```{=html}

The `hypotheses()` function uses the model's estimated covariance matrix, so it works naturally with `PyFixest` objects. ::: {#4a6d53b3 .cell execution_count=4} ``` {.python .cell-code} hypotheses(fit, "X1 - X2 = 0") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=4} ```{=html}

Here is a simple OLS example: ::: {#fbec5ea8 .cell execution_count=5} ``` {.python .cell-code} fit_ols = pf.feols("Y ~ X1 + X2", data=data) ``` ::: ::: {#906dbad3 .cell execution_count=6} ``` {.python .cell-code} hypotheses(fit_ols, "(X1 / Intercept - 1) * 100 = 0") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=6} ```{=html}
